public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI companies are predominantly unprofitable, perpetually searching for product-market fit, and even when they find it seem incapable of generating revenue that remotely justifies their valuations.

statement.excerpt: These companies are predominantly unprofitable, perpetually searching for product-market fit, and even when they find it, seem incapable of generating revenue numbers that remotely justify their valuations.

from_speaker: seem incapable of generating revenue numbers that remotely justify their valuations
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading of predominantly unprofitable is that most companies in the discussed group lose money overall, counted by company rather than weighted by revenue or valuation.
These companies refers to the generative AI businesses discussed in the surrounding passage. The passage does not establish a complete population or sampling rule.

For the ongoing profitability observation, use January–March 2025, the latest completed calendar quarter that could have been reported before the June 30 post. This reporting-period choice is supplied by the evaluator.
Read unprofitable as negative net income. Cash burn, operating losses and gross margins are different measures.
The surrounding financial discussion relies on press estimates, so estimate is the indicated evidence basis; no common accounting standard is specified.
Read perpetually searching as continued difficulty establishing sustained customer demand, not a literal prediction covering all future time.
The valuation clause expresses doubt about whether sales support the prices investors pay. No revenue multiple, growth assumption or fair-value method is supplied, and none is invented here.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable net-income evidence must show that more than half of a defensibly defined population of the companies discussed lost money during the target quarter. The other clauses require evidence of persistent difficulty sustaining customer demand and a stated, defensible standard connecting revenue to valuation; revenue and valuation figures alone cannot establish that valuations are unjustified.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence that at least half of the defined population earned nonnegative net income would contradict the majority-loss assertion. Broad evidence of sustained commercial demand would weigh against the product-market-fit assertion. A single profitable company does not contradict predominantly, and a high valuation does not by itself prove or disprove the valuation judgment.

evidence.locator: Section 'Keeping us in food and clothes', David Holz quotation
evidence.explanation: A company named in the post had publicly claimed profitability. This historical exception cautions against treating losses as universal, but does not establish its 2025 finances or contradict a majority claim.

evidence.excerpt: Anthropic has raised $3.5 billion at a $61.5 billion post-money valuation.
evidence.explanation: Establishes a financing valuation during the target quarter. It provides neither net income nor a test of whether revenue justifies that valuation; financing proceeds are not revenue.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A defined company population and comparable target-quarter net-income records sufficient to establish whether most lost money would resolve the profitability component. The remaining clauses require explicit standards for sustained customer demand and revenue-supported valuation before they can receive a fair binary assessment.
